hero.lead: A nation of 25.2 million whose revised mining code and resolved gold dispute set growth near 5.5% for 2026, with public debt of 41.9% of GDP.

capital.heading: Gold under a new code. Next, the price.

record.text: Total public debt of the central government, share of GDP, 2025 (estimate), down from 44.0% in 2024 and projected at 40.8% in 2026 (second review of the Staff-Monitored Program, July 2026)
State spending in the amended finance law for 2026, up from XOF 3,578.2 billion in the initial law; revenue XOF 3,372.9 billion and a deficit of XOF 620.4 billion
Infrastructure a mining-backed fund could unlock, from the 2023 mining code
IMF Rapid Credit Facility, SDR 93.3 million (50% of quota), disbursed at once on approval on 16 April 2025, for urgent balance of payments needs after the floods
Real growth expected to rebound to about 5.5% in 2026, after 4.9% projected for 2025; fiscal deficit projected by IMF staff at 2.4% of GDP in 2026 (July 2026)

register.name: State budget 2026, amended finance law
register.detail: Amended in 2026 · expenditure XOF 3,993.319 billion · revenue XOF 3,372.895 billion · deficit XOF 620.425 billion
register.note: Spending of the State in 2026, up 11.6% on the initial law
register.text: The amended law raised spending from XOF 3,578.2 billion in the initial 2026 law. It pays for the public services behind all seven standards.

register.name: Mali Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
register.detail: Presented in Bamako, 5 February 2026 · 3.8 million people targeted of 5.1 million in need · about 28% less than in 2025
register.note: Requirement of the 2026 plan; APA News later reported $577.9M, 23% funded at 28 September 2026
register.text: Food, health, water, shelter and protection for people hit by conflict and displacement. It serves Food, Water, Health and Shelter.

register.name: Mining-backed infrastructure fund
register.detail: Government of Mali · Announced August 2026
register.note: Announced in August 2026, as reported by Mining Weekly
register.text: A fund backed by mining revenue that, the Government says, could unlock up to $800 million for infrastructure projects. It would draw on the windfall from the 2023 mining code to build the roads, power and water behind the seven standards.

register.name: Treasury bills and bonds on the regional market (UMOA-Titres)
register.detail: State of Mali · Auction of 10 June 2026, value date 11 June 2026 · 364-day bills, 3-year and 5-year bonds
register.note: XOF 50 billion offered; bids of XOF 88.76 billion; XOF 55 billion retained
register.text: A public auction of Treasury securities by the State of Mali on the regional market of the West African Monetary Union, run by UMOA-Titres. Bids reached XOF 88.76 billion for XOF 50 billion offered, and XOF 55 billion was retained. It is borrowing in CFA francs, on the regional market.

register.name: Emergency Access to Essential Services Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Credit approved 26 March 2026 · health and education
register.note: 2.3 million people with access to essential health services; 1.1 million students supported
register.text: An IDA credit that pays the operational costs of health facilities, essential vaccines and medicines, and free care for women of reproductive age and children under five. In schools it provides teaching materials, grants to the most vulnerable students and the organisation of national examinations. It serves the health and education standards.

register.name: Staff-Monitored Program
register.detail: IMF · Approved March 2025 · 11 months · second and final review approved by IMF Management 18 March 2026
register.note: Inflation below 3 percent, as in 2025
register.text: An 11-month programme with IMF staff, requested with the Rapid Credit Facility of April 2025 to re-establish a track record. IMF Management approved its second and final review on 18 March 2026; the 2026 budget envisages a fiscal deficit within the West African Economic and Monetary Union ceiling of 3 percent of GDP.

register.name: Road Infrastructure Connectivity and Resilience Improvement Program (Mali-NSS)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Credit approved, release of 28 May 2025 · about CFAF 133 billion · 137.7 km Diéma–Sandaré section
register.note: One million people within 150 km of the road to benefit indirectly
register.text: An IDA credit to rehabilitate and upgrade the 137.7 km Diéma–Sandaré section of the Bamako–Dakar Northern Corridor to climate-resilient standards. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Rapid Credit Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved 16 April 2025 · SDR 93.3 million, 50% of quota · disbursed at once
register.note: Accompanied by an 11-month Staff-Monitored Program
register.text: Emergency IMF financing to help the authorities meet urgent balance of payments needs resulting from the floods of 2024. The full amount, SDR 93.3 million, was disbursed on approval.

register.name: Bamako Urban Resilience Project (PRUBA), additional financing
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Additional financing announced 1 April 2025 · $100 million for Mali and Chad, $50 million each
register.note: Replenishes the project after US$73 million was released through its emergency component
register.text: Additional IDA financing to replenish the Bamako Urban Resilience Project, whose contingent emergency response component released US$73 million immediately after the floods of 2024. More than 370,000 people were affected, and nearly 300 schools and 35 health centres were flooded and damaged. It serves the shelter standard, where 92.5% of city dwellers live in slums.

register.name: Mali Water Security Support Project (PASEMa)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Credit approved, release of 22 January 2025 · Bamako and secondary towns
register.note: About 500,000 people to benefit; 227,000 to gain at least basic water services
register.text: An IDA credit to help Mali increase access to drinking water and improve the conservation of water sources in Bamako and secondary towns. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Community Resilience and Revitalizing Access to Essential Services Project (Malidenko)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Credit approved, release of 14 November 2024 · six regions, 57 communes, 850 villages
register.note: 1.84 million people to have access to improved basic services
register.text: An IDA credit that uses a community-driven approach to deliver basic services in fragile areas and to strengthen the link between the State and citizens. It includes measures for poor women, youth, internally displaced persons and persons with disabilities, and reaches several of the seven standards at once.

register.name: Advancing Resilience and Inclusive Health Systems for Everyone in Mali (Keneya Yiriwali)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Credit approved, release of 28 June 2024 · $100 million IDA credit and $25 million Global Financing Facility grant
register.note: 15.4 million women, adolescent girls and children to benefit
register.text: A health operation that uses results-based financing to improve the quality of essential health services, particularly reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, adolescent and nutrition services. It serves the health standard, where the WHO service coverage index stands at 41.

register.name: Bamako North 225 kV Loop Project
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved 12 November 2025 · loan agreements signed 25 February 2026 · ratification bill adopted by the National Transitional Council (release of 2 July 2026) · total cost $190 million
register.note: ADF loan $35.27M, Transition Support Facility loan $18.99M, Climate Investment Funds $5M loan and $6.8M grant, Green Climate Fund $2.2M grant
register.text: A 225 kV line between the Kodialani and Dialakorobougou substations, two new substations at Safo and Kénié and extensions to three others, raising transmission capacity for Bamako to 600 megawatts. It is to connect 10,000 new households and small businesses to the grid, with BOAD and the Islamic Development Bank as co-financiers. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Tiètiguila solar power plant, 50 MWp with battery storage
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st meeting of the Board of Directors, Lomé, 26 June 2026 · 25 MW/50 MWh of battery energy storage
register.note: XOF 44.368 billion to the Republic of Mali
register.text: BOAD financing for a 50 MWp solar photovoltaic power plant with 25 MW/50 MWh of battery storage at Tiètiguila. It will increase the share of renewable energy in the national energy mix and secure electricity coverage, which serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: School Infrastructure Strengthening Project, Phase I
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st meeting of the Board of Directors, Lomé, 26 June 2026
register.note: To the Republic of Mali
register.text: BOAD financing for the construction, rehabilitation and equipping of educational facilities, to expand access to quality education. It serves the education standard, where 9.6% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school on the last measure.

register.name: Electricity transmission grid modernisation and expansion
register.detail: IsDB · Approved at the 353rd meeting of the Board of Executive Directors, release of 10 December 2023 · high-voltage transmission
register.note: US$58.0 million at approval
register.text: Islamic Development Bank financing to enhance the electricity transmission grid of Mali by modernising and expanding its high-voltage transmission infrastructure. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach.

register.name: Refinancing facility for BSIC SA Mali
register.detail: BOAD · Approved at the 151st meeting of the Board of Directors, Lomé, 26 June 2026 · Banque Sahélo-Saharienne pour l’Investissement et le Commerce Mali
register.note: For medium-term loans to small businesses, green investments and women-led firms
register.text: BOAD refinancing for a commercial bank, to support medium-term loans to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, promote green investments and expand access to finance for women-owned and women-led businesses. It serves the livelihood standard, where 45.5% live below the national poverty line.

register.name: SDN Flour Mill Project
register.detail: IFC · Approved on an absence-of-objection basis, 20 May 2026 · senior secured loans · IDA21 Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility
register.note: An A loan of up to €6.5 million for IFC’s own account and concessional loans of up to €4.875 million and €1.625 million
register.text: Senior secured loans of up to €13 million to Societe Diarra Negoce for a flour mill, part of them concessional finance from the IDA21 Private Sector Window. It serves the food standard, where 20.6% of Malians are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: Mali solar rural electrification project
register.detail: GCF FP102 · Approved 28 February 2019 · BOAD · loan and grant · 4% disbursed · completion estimated 10 February 2027
register.note: Total project value $38.4 million, with $9.3 million of co-financing
register.text: GCF financing, through BOAD, for 4.83 megawatts of isolated solar photovoltaic mini-grids in 50 rural communities. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach, where 49.5% have electricity.

register.name: Global Fund grants for HIV, tuberculosis and malaria
register.detail: Signed 15 March 2024 · three grants · with the Government of Mali, ARCAD Santé PLUS and Plan International Mali
register.note: Three grants signed together
register.text: Continues the fight against HIV, tuberculosis and malaria and strengthens the health system. It serves Health.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Gold
items.label: State stake allowed under the 2023 mining code
items.text: Gold carries exports; the code raises the nation’s share, now to be turned into roads, power and schools.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: The inner Niger delta and the savannah: farmland that can feed the Sahel.

items.name: The Ground
items.label: Of GDP from natural resource rents, 2021
items.text: What lies under the land already earns; the task is to turn the rent into lasting assets.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 45.8% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: myAgro
items.text: A social enterprise whose mobile layaway platform lets farmers save by phone over six to eight months for farm inputs, with prices locked in at the outset. In 2025 it served more than 250,000 farmers across Senegal, Mali and Côte d’Ivoire, 65 percent of them women.

items.name: La Voûte Nubienne (AVN)
items.text: An association that trains apprentices, masons and entrepreneurs to build with Nubian Vault earth-brick roofs. Since 2007 its programme in Mali has completed more than 3,000 projects for the benefit of more than 25,000 people.

items.name: Africa GreenTec
items.text: A green mini-grid developer whose Malian subsidiary, Africa GreenTec Électrification Rurale, produces, distributes and sells renewable energy in 20 communities. In January 2024 CEI Africa Foundation awarded it up to USD 1,953,000 in results-based financing to build seven new mini-grids in rural Mali and extend 18 others.

items.name: Kabakoo Academies
items.text: Founded in Mali in 2018, it runs blended, project-based cohorts for young people that combine mobile learning, community hubs and peer collaboration. It has over 34,000 registered learners.

items.name: OKO
items.text: A company providing crop-specific parametric climate insurance to farmers, with premiums and claims handled through mobile money; in Mali it is part of the Orange Money menu. To date it has insured 33,341 farmers and compensated 8,596, paying USD 482K in claims.
